triage_context.environment: Unknown. Treat any externally-reachable entry point as untrusted; flag trust-boundary assumptions explicitly in rationale. (Per THREAT_MODEL.md: internet-facing SPA + Supabase PostgREST/Edge Functions; any authenticated employee account is untrusted relative to stores/permissions it was not granted.)

findings.title: Full CPF recoverable via cpf_mascarado + localizar_colaborador_por_cpf oracle by roles without dados_pessoais.ler
preconditions: Authenticated employee session (function revoked from anon)
Holds colaborador.ler for the target's current store (gerente_loja or supervisor)
Lacks colaborador.dados_pessoais.ler but can read cpf_mascarado (middle 6 digits -> 1,000 candidates)
No rate limit / MFA step-up / per-call audit on rpc/localizar_colaborador_por_cpf (~1,000 calls per target)
findings.rationale:
localizar_colaborador_por_cpf (20261023001400_classificacao_ia.sql:35-45) is SECURITY DEFINER, granted to authenticated, matches raw c.cpf and requires only colaborador.ler (no MFA, 20261023000700_dashboard_seeds.sql:54), so it confirms the correct guess without an audit record. gerente_loja (dashboard_seeds.sql:117) and supervisor (20261023001600_perfil_supervisor.sql:15) hold colaborador.ler but not colaborador.dados_pessoais.ler, and can read cpf_mascarado (20261023000500_pessoas_regras_rls.sql:11-12,19), which exposes digits 4-9 so only 1,000 valid candidates remain. They bypass the MFA-gated, audited colaborador_dados_pessoais path (pessoas_regras_rls.sql:176-186); no later migration, revoke or rate limit closes the gap.

The SECURITY DEFINER RPC matches on raw cpf and checks only colaborador.ler, so a store manager can brute-force the 3 hidden leading digits of a coworker's CPF and recover the full number, bypassing the MFA-gated, audited colaborador_dados_pessoais path. Requires an authenticated role and only reaches employees of stores the attacker already manages, ~1,000 calls each: MEDIUM rather than HIGH, but it is LGPD-regulated personal data and should be prioritized.
findings.owner_hint: component: supabase/migrations/; no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer Diego Bonfim (1/1 recent commits) — owner: Diego Bonfim (Idealize RH)
findings.recommendation: Require privado.pode('colaborador.dados_pessoais.ler', loja) in the RPC (or revoke from authenticated and call it with service role from the edge function after checks); audit each lookup; consider a stronger mask.

findings.title: documentos_editar UPDATE policy lets enviar-holders forge attribution, signature status and dates on approved documents
preconditions: Valid active account calling PostgREST directly (PATCH /rest/v1/documentos)
Holds documento.<nivel>.enviar for the document's category and store (e.g. gerente_loja/supervisor via documento.geral.enviar)
Target document is in a category/store the attacker already has upload rights for (loja/categoria locked by trigger)
findings.rationale:
The documentos_editar policy (20261023000600_documentos.sql:147-149) gives table-wide UPDATE to anyone with enviar permission for that category and store, and no migration revokes or narrows UPDATE on public.documentos (line 157 revokes only insert and delete). travar_documento (lines 113-122) locks only status, conferido_por, versao_atual, loja_id, colaborador_id and categoria_id, so a direct PostgREST PATCH can rewrite enviado_por, criado_por, conferido_em, status_assinatura and vencimento on an approved document without resetting approval. The comment at line 146 limits intended edits to name, dates and notes, so attribution and signature fields are not covered by intended design. The audit trigger (line 95) only records the change.

A store-scoped employee with upload rights but no documento.conferir can rewrite enviado_por, criado_por, conferido_em, status_assinatura and vencimento on an already-approved document without resetting approval, faking authorship, signature state, or hiding expiries from dashboard counters. Needs login plus a per-store permission and is confined to the attacker's own store/category; the auditar trigger logs every change. MEDIUM, matching the scanner.
findings.owner_hint: component: supabase/migrations/; no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer Diego Bonfim (1/1 recent commits) — owner: Diego Bonfim (Idealize RH)
findings.recommendation: Revoke UPDATE on documentos from authenticated and grant UPDATE only on (nome, observacoes) or extend travar_documento to all integrity columns; ignore status_assinatura from p_meta.

findings.title: tarefas UPDATE policy lets assignee move a task to any store and forge origem/concluida_por/chave_dedup
preconditions: A manager already assigned the attacker as responsavel_id on an existing task (insert needs tarefa.gerir)
Knows the target store's loja_id UUID
chave_dedup squatting only matters once system task generation exists (not yet)
findings.rationale:
The WITH CHECK of tarefas_editar (20261023000400_auditoria_timeline_tarefas.sql:172-174) accepts any new row where responsavel_id = auth.uid(), without checking tarefa.gerir on the new loja_id and without the origem='manual' rule the insert policy enforces (line 165). No column revokes for authenticated, no replacement policy and no blocking trigger exist (only timestamp, uppercase and audit). An assignee can PATCH a task into another store with origem='sistema' and a forged title, visible via tarefas_ler (line 162), and can squat a unique chave_dedup (line 132).

The WITH CHECK on tarefas_editar lets an assignee move their task into any store with origem='sistema' and any title; nothing blocks it and auditar only records it. Impact is limited to integrity of one task record (fake 'system' task in another store's queue, or future dedup-key squatting); no data read or privilege gained. LOW, matching the scanner.
findings.owner_hint: component: supabase/migrations/; no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer Diego Bonfim (1/1 recent commits) — owner: Diego Bonfim (Idealize RH)
findings.recommendation: Require tarefa.gerir in the new loja_id in WITH CHECK; trigger locking origem, chave_dedup, criado_por; server-set concluida_por; validate colaborador store.

findings.title: Upload RPCs callable directly: file-less 'confirmed' versions with forged hash/MIME; confirm can roll back or un-archive documents
preconditions: Authenticated employee calling rpc/documento_confirmar_upload directly or via the edge function
Passes pode_documento('enviar', categoria, loja) at both prepare and confirm
Attacker started the still-unconfirmed version themselves (enviado_por = auth.uid())
For the un-archive impact: a separate privileged user archived the document between prepare and confirm
findings.rationale:
documento_confirmar_upload (supabase/migrations/20261023000600_documentos.sql:233-257) is granted to authenticated (lines 343-352) and callable directly via PostgREST. It never checks that the storage object exists, the document status, or that v.versao > versao_atual, and it sets status='recebido' clearing the review fields. The archived check exists only at prepare time (line 216), so an uploader without documento.arquivar (required at line 304) can prepare a version, wait for archiving, then confirm it to un-archive the document with no file behind it. The promised 24 h cleanup of unconfirmed versions (line 165) does not exist.

The harmful case (un-archiving without documento.arquivar) needs an authenticated user with enviar on the category/store, a self-created pending version, and an intervening archive by someone else: 3+ preconditions, LOW. The shorter path (a confirmed version with no file and client-supplied hash/MIME) gains little over uploading junk. Impact is confined to documents the attacker can already write; scanner MEDIUM is one level inflated.
findings.owner_hint: component: supabase/migrations/; no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer Diego Bonfim (1/1 recent commits) — owner: Diego Bonfim (Idealize RH)
findings.recommendation: Revoke both RPCs from authenticated and call them from the edge function with service role passing the verified user id; in confirm reject archived docs and stale versions and check storage.objects.

findings.title: PDF active-content regex filter bypassable (#xx name escapes, compressed object streams, unlisted /AA /URI /SubmitForm)
findings.rationale: The regex at supabase/functions/_shared/comum.ts:57 really is bypassable, but it is a best-effort hardening filter on an upload path restricted to authenticated users with enviar permission (20261023000600_documentos.sql:185/213). Files are served from the supabase.co origin through 60 s signed URLs (documentos-acesso/index.ts:33), so they cannot run script in the app origin; harm needs a desktop PDF reader that runs actions without prompting. Missing hardening only (rule 13); already tracked in THREAT_MODEL.md section 8.
findings.recommendation: Parse with a real PDF library (inflate streams, normalize names) and reject active keys, or flatten/re-render PDFs server-side; serve with download disposition.

findings.title: Per-user MFA flag makes every exige_mfa permission (incl. acesso.gerir) password-only for all non-owner accounts
findings.rationale: sessao_aal2() at 20261023001800_mfa_por_usuario.sql:19 does let users without mfa_obrigatorio pass exige_mfa checks at AAL1, but the migration header (lines 3-6) records it as the owner's explicit decision and supabase/tests/80_mfa_por_usuario.sql:11-18 asserts it; THREAT_MODEL.md T1 already tracks the residual risk. The escalation sub-claim belongs to the access-grant policy, not this code.
findings.recommendation: Keep the per-user relaxation but exclude the access-control plane: acesso.gerir (and ideally auditoria.ler) must always require a real aal2; or auto-force mfa_obrigatorio=true for holders of profiles with acesso.gerir.

findings.title: Access-management has no grant ceiling and no protection of the owner (revoke / disable owner's MFA)
findings.rationale: Only diretoria and rh_central hold acesso.gerir and both get every permission (20261023000700_dashboard_seeds.sql:95-99), so granting diretoria from rh_central gives no privilege the caller lacks. Managing other users' MFA and assignments is the documented design (20261023001800_mfa_por_usuario.sql:3-6, tested in tests/80_mfa_por_usuario.sql). Owner protection and grant expiry ceilings are hardening that only matters if rh_central is meant to be less trusted than the owner.
findings.recommendation: Only diretoria (at aal2) may grant diretoria/rh_central/acesso.gerir or act on diretoria holders; cap valido_ate at caller's own; never allow mfa_obrigatorio=false for acesso.gerir holders.

findings.title: cadastrar_colaborador / atualizar_dados_pessoais reveal CPF existence across stores
findings.rationale: The duplicate check at 20261023000500_pessoas_regras_rls.sql:118-120 mirrors the group-wide unique key on colaboradores.cpf (20261023000300_pessoas_vinculos.sql:31), which would surface the same 23505 error on insert anyway; one person per CPF across the group (re-hire flow) is the intended design. It needs colaborador.criar and reveals one bit about a CPF the caller already holds, with no name/store/id.
findings.recommendation: Return a generic error for cross-store duplicates; catch unique_violation and raise a generic message.

findings.title: registrar_sugestao_ia lets any active user write arbitrary CLASSIFICACAO_IA audit entries for any store
findings.rationale: registrar_sugestao_ia (classificacao_ia.sql:48-65) is self-reported telemetry the edge function calls with the user's own JWT (index.ts:186). audit_log.usuario_id defaults to auth.uid() (auditoria_timeline_tarefas.sql:11), so every row names the true caller, and the log is append-only (lines 30-33). The only effect is attributable noise tagged with another store id: low-impact nuisance (rule 12); a loja_id check is hardening.
findings.recommendation: Revoke from authenticated; record from the edge function with service role, or require documento.*.enviar and validate loja_id access.

findings.title: transferir_colaborador validates before authorizing -> store-location oracle for any employee UUID
findings.rationale: The pre-authorization branches at 20261023000500_pessoas_regras_rls.sql:248-249 do run before privado.exigir (251-252), but using the oracle requires the random UUID of an employee hidden by RLS (colaboradores_ler, lines 38-39) and the output is only which of ~4 stores they work at, with no data or write access. Low-impact nuisance; reordering exigir is a cheap hardening.
findings.recommendation: Authorize right after existence check; return a generic error.

findings.title: Timeline gates document titles by the employee's current store, not the document's store
findings.rationale: timeline_ler (20261023000400_auditoria_timeline_tarefas.sql:157) gates by the employee's current store while documentos_ler gates by the document's store; they only diverge after a transfer, and the reader must hold the same documento.<sigilo>.ler for that employee at the current store. The timeline is employee-scoped by design (Manual.tsx:263/340), only the title is exposed, and the financeiro/remuneracao.ler substitution is explicit in pode_sigilo (line 111).
findings.recommendation: Gate document-linked timeline rows by the document's permission; avoid free-text titles for sensitive sigilo.

findings.title: documento_arquivar does not check the category sigilo permission
findings.rationale: documento_arquivar (documentos.sql:304) does skip the sigilo check and departamento_pessoal has arquivar without juridico.ler (dashboard_seeds.sql:107-112), but exploitation needs the random UUID of a document the user cannot read; the claimed timeline leak is closed by timeline_ler's pode_sigilo filter (auditoria_timeline_tarefas.sql:156-157) and all document tables are RLS-gated. Missing defense-in-depth only.

findings.title: status_transicoes writable by admin_tecnico (config.estrutura.gerir), rewriting the employment state machine
findings.rationale: status_transicoes is documented as a configurable state machine (20261023000300_pessoas_vinculos.sql:99) and the named policies at 20261023000500_pessoas_regras_rls.sql:63-66 deliberately give it to config.estrutura.gerir (admin_tecnico's stated role). admin_tecnico lacks vinculo.status.alterar, so any reopened contract still needs a separately authorized, audited HR action.
findings.recommendation: Revoke writes from authenticated; protect terminal states with a trigger.

findings.title: Any new auth user becomes an active usuarios row with self-chosen name if public signup is enabled
findings.rationale: The trigger (20261023000800_auth_storage.sql:8-25) deliberately creates an active usuarios row with no assignments (comment lines 5-7); real permissions need usuario_atribuicoes (acesso_rbac.sql:82/104/128). Exploitation needs public signup enabled, which README.md:66 requires disabling and the owner reports disabled; what remains is social engineering an admin. Missing hardening only.
findings.recommendation: Keep signup disabled (verify); create usuarios only for invited users (invited_at not null) or with ativo=false.

findings.title: Uniform ledger sum cast to integer can overflow, bricking an item and the stock view
findings.rationale: The integer cast in saldo_uniforme (20261023001500_uniformes.sql:100) can overflow with no upper bound on quantidade (001700:94), but entrada requires uniforme.estoque (001700:79), granted only to diretoria/rh_central/departamento_pessoal (001700:15-18), trusted central roles that already control stock data. Availability nuisance in a non-sensitive module; cap quantidade as hardening.
findings.recommendation: Cap quantidade (e.g. 1..100000) and compute in bigint.

findings.title: LLM suggestions pre-fill category/employee and batch upload sends them in one click
findings.rationale: AI output only pre-fills editable fields shown with an 'AI suggestion' badge, confidence, reason and 'Confira antes de enviar' (EnvioDocumentos.tsx:227,296,317); category is a server-checked closed list (documentos-classificar/index.ts:102,151), employee matching runs under the uploader's JWT (161,165), upload permission is re-checked server-side (documentos-upload/index.ts:52) and documents land as 'recebido' pending review (68).
findings.recommendation: Require per-item confirmation when AI chose employee or a lower sigilo; never let AI lower sigilo silently.

findings.title: Password change needs only the session (no current password / reauth)
findings.rationale: trocarSenha (Admin.tsx:387-397) calls updateUser without re-auth, but exploitation requires an already-stolen session token that already grants full access; the attacker could call /auth/v1/user directly, so the control is Supabase's server-side 'secure password change' setting, not visible in the repo. Missing hardening.
findings.recommendation: Enable secure password change / reauthenticate nonce; signOut others after change.

findings.title: Invite redirect falls back to the request Origin header when SITE_URL is unset
findings.rationale: The Origin fallback (index.ts:35) is reachable only by acesso.gerir holders (17-22), Supabase discards redirectTo values outside the exact allowlist, and the invitee starts with no access (2-4). Requiring SITE_URL is hardening.

findings.title: privado SECURITY DEFINER helpers executable by authenticated; only reachable if privado schema is exposed
findings.rationale: The EXECUTE grants are required because RLS policies and the security_invoker view call these helpers (perfil_supervisor.sql:57,71-77; pessoas_vinculos.sql:227-228). privado is not exposed via PostgREST (default public/graphql_public; no config override). Missing hardening dependent on a hypothetical config change.
findings.recommendation: Keep privado unexposed; revoke EXECUTE where not needed.
